(a) Facility and Infrastructure Policy.—
        (1) In general.—The Secretary shall develop and implement a strategy for facilities and infrastructure supported primarily from the Office of Science, the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, the Office of Fossil Energy, or the Office of Nuclear Energy, Science and Technology Programs at all National Laboratories and single-purpose research facilities.  
        (2) Strategy.—The strategy shall provide cost-effective means for—
            (A) maintaining existing facilities and infrastructure;  
            (B) closing unneeded facilities;  
            (C) making facility modifications; and  
            (D) building new facilities.    
    (b) Report.—
        (1) In general.—The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2008, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).  
        (2) Contents.—For each National Laboratory and single-purpose research facility that is primarily used for science and energy research, the report shall contain—
            (A) the current priority list of proposed facilities and infrastructure projects, including cost and schedule requirements;  
            (B) a current 10-year plan that demonstrates the reconfiguration of its facilities and infrastructure to meet its missions and to address its long-term operational costs and return on investment;  
            (C) the total current budget for all facilities and infrastructure funding; and  
            (D) the current status of each facility and infrastructure project compared to the original baseline cost, schedule, and scope.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that developing a strategy and submitting a report are procedural steps that amount to participation. But the Secretary develops the strategy alone, and the only interaction is a report to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The section requires no consultation with states, experts, the public, or other outside parties, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2008, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary to develop a strategy and submit a report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities before making the decision.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2008, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).

opus.w: The Secretary develops the facilities strategy alone and reports it to Congress, which is part of the federal government. The section does not call for consulting states, experts, industry or the public, and it does not provide for an advisory body, a comment period or rulemaking. The report requirement might look procedural, but a report to Congress stays inside the federal government, so it is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2008, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to develop a strategy and submit a report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is internal government communication, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with non-federal entities, or involvement of an advisory board with outside members.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2008, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "strategy" or "plan" involves input from outside parties, but the text only mandates the Secretary to develop the strategy and submit a report to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and the development of the strategy by the Secretary is an internal executive branch action. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes/public.
